steps.name: Run on this branch and the base

run.head_commit_message:
fix(formation): read and write the unit store once a pass (Decision 144) (#229)

* fix(formation): passes read units' places once instead of per unit

Step 4's bench showed 4a's scattered place reads costing 22.6% on the
Rust engine (deaths, blows, the re-form's occupancy, units walking to
places): each UnitPlace.of or rank was two store reads, and under Rust
each read is a call into the field. UnitPlace.table fetches a squad's
ranks and columns once and UnitPlace.read reads a unit's place from
them. fighters(), ranged combat, SquadCompact (which now commits its
ranks once), the march's distances and pour targets, the re-form's
occupancy and front-first order, SquadEdges, SquadGeometry, the trade,
SquadRanks and the back-row counts fetch once a pass. No outcome
changes.

Tests: test_unit_place.gd checks a table reads each place as the store
holds it on both backends (red on 4e's UnitPlace).

Waived-by: Decision 142

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YWpV2AHWr3d2v4fKRki8G7

* docs(spec): record step 4's bench and the place-read fix's

Step 4 with the fix against main before it: 353.2 to 281.6 ms a tick
(-20.3%); the fix alone, 315.9 to 283.1 (-10.4%). 4a alone had cost
22.6%, and 4a to 4e 2.9%, before the fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YWpV2AHWr3d2v4fKRki8G7

* fix(formation): passes write the store once, not unit by unit

Body parting's write-back is now the field's own: BodyField.commit_part
writes every moved body into the store's columns once GDScript has
loosened the units parting made loose, instead of four puts a unit
from GDScript. The march's write-back puts the routers', loose and
placed points into fetched columns and commits them once, then the
units in their places walk. The native walk's paying for the ground
moves to ScrumWalkField.pay and fetches and commits once. The other
loops that read the store unit by unit are marked with why: per-event
loops, the GDScript reference's own seek, walk and facing, and the
rout's, pursuit's and regroup's per-unit steps, small at the bench.
No outcome changes.

Waived-by: Decision 142

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YWpV2AHWr3d2v4fKRki8G7

* chore(ci): check that no loop reads the unit store unit by unit

check_store_reads.py flags, in sim/, a scattered store call written in
a loop's body (columns.value/put, UnitPlace.of/rank/put,
SquadEntries.loose_at, EntryKeys.*) unless the line or its loop is
marked '# store: scattered (<why>)'. Run by pre-commit and CI, with
its tests; its heuristic limit (reads hidden in helpers) is stated in
ci/godot/README.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YWpV2AHWr3d2v4fKRki8G7

* docs(principles): a pass reads the unit store once (Decision 144)

bounded-work.md gains Principle 3: a loop over units never reads or
writes the store one unit at a time; helpers take an optional fetched
table; scattered reads are marked with their reason. Recorded as
Decision 144 and added to the design-check skill. Spec 35's steps 5 to
7 each begin with a readers list and a fetch-once plan, and the bench
against the base must show no phase slower. OPEN_QUESTIONS Q24 lists
the per-tick passes that could become work lists fed by events.

Deaths and the re-form's occupancy came in above main on this runner;
